did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with a father’s personal appeal to his son: it is not enough to hear words of wisdom; you must accept them and keep the commandments in your heart and in your life.
Wisdom is described as a treasure to be sought diligently, like silver and hidden riches. This image emphasizes that wisdom requires effort, persistence, and attention.

According to the chapter, seeking wisdom leads to understanding the fear of the LORD and finding the knowledge of God. Here, the fear of the LORD is presented as a deep and respectful acknowledgment of God.
The verse emphasizes that the source of wisdom is the LORD: people ask, listen, and search, but the LORD is the one who gives wisdom, knowledge, and understanding.
Wisdom is not merely theoretical knowledge. It also includes practical insight, and the LORD is described as a shield for those who walk with integrity and as the guardian of the ways of justice.
When wisdom enters the heart and knowledge becomes pleasing to the soul, they no longer remain external ideas but become part of a person’s inner life.
The chapter presents understanding as a means of rescue: it protects people from those who speak perversely, abandon what is right, and choose evil ways.
Wisdom is also described as protection from the temptation of an immoral woman—that is, a figure who uses flattering words and leads a person away from faithfulness to the covenant.
The purpose of the chapter’s instruction is practical: to walk in the way of the good and follow the paths of the righteous, rather than merely understanding wisdom.
At the end of the chapter, a clear distinction is made between two ways: the upright and blameless will remain in the land, while the wicked and treacherous will be cut off from it.
